stem: During pre-transplant evaluation counseling, a candidate with severe obesity asks whether weight affects transplant eligibility. Which teaching point aligns with standard contraindication references?

options.text: Severe obesity may be a contraindication to transplantation
Obesity has no effect on transplant candidacy at any level
Only underweight candidates are evaluated for contraindications

explanation.rationale_correct: Nutritional evaluation identifies obesity as a comorbidity that, if severe, may be a contraindication to transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Obesity is specifically addressed as a comorbidity that can affect candidacy.
rationale_incorrect.C: Both overweight and underweight candidates undergo nutritional assessment for transplant suitability.
rationale_incorrect.D: Obesity is a comorbidity reviewed for candidacy rather than an automatic priority boost.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Obesity is considered a comorbidity and, if severe, may be a contraindication to transplantation

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → H. Nutritional evaluation → 1.a.i. (severe obesity may be a contraindication); PDF p. 32 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Seventh 010200 item; obesity-contraindication angle distinct from smoking risks (cctc-1034/1037); anchor verified on Cupples p. 32.

stem: A recipient asks whether soft cheeses from a local farm are safe after transplant. Which dietary teaching aligns with standard infection-prevention references?

options.text: Avoid unpasteurized milk and products made from unpasteurized milk such as certain soft cheeses
All unpasteurized dairy products are encouraged for immune support
Only meat restrictions apply; dairy requires no precautions
Soft cheeses are safe regardless of pasteurization status

explanation.rationale_correct: Dietary infection-prevention teaching includes avoiding unpasteurized foods, including milk and products made from unpasteurized milk such as certain soft cheeses.

rationale_incorrect.B: Unpasteurized dairy increases foodborne infection risk and is not recommended.
rationale_incorrect.C: Dietary precautions include unpasteurized dairy as well as undercooked meat and seafood.
rationale_incorrect.D: Pasteurization status matters; unpasteurized soft cheeses should be avoided.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention → iii. Dietary precautions
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Do not consume unpasteurized foods including … Products made from unpasteurized milk (e.g., certain soft cheeses)

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → e. Infection prevention → iii. Dietary precautions (avoid unpasteurized milk and soft cheeses); PDF p. 116 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Tenth 010600 item; unpasteurized-dairy angle distinct from live-virus household contact (cctc-1046) and vaccination combo (cctc-1048); anchor verified on Cupples p. 116.

stem: A coordinator is updating dietary infection-prevention teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Recipients should not eat raw seed sprouts.
Bagged lettuce labeled pre-washed should still be washed before eating.
Raw or undercooked meat and seafood are safe for immunosuppressed recipients.
Unpasteurized fruit or vegetable juices should be avoided.

explanation.rationale_correct: Dietary teaching advises against raw sprouts, unpasteurized juices, and raw or undercooked meat and seafood, and recommends washing bagged lettuce even when labeled pre-washed.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also correct—unpasteurized juices should be avoided.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statements I and II are also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false; raw or undercooked meat and seafood are not safe.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention → iii. Dietary precautions
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Do not eat raw seed sprouts … Wash bagged lettuce … Do not consume unpasteurized … fruit or vegetable juices

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → e. Infection prevention → iii. Dietary precautions (sprouts, bagged lettuce washing, unpasteurized juices, raw meat/seafood); PDF p. 116 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Synthesized item. Tenth complex_combo in bank; distinct from infection-prevention combo (cctc-1024); anchor verified on Cupples p. 116.

stem: A recipient planning to use a hotel hot tub after discharge asks about infection risk. What teaching aligns with standard post-transplant infection-prevention references?

options.text: Follow transplant program guidance on hot tubs, tap water, and related environmental exposures
Hot tubs are universally safe without any program-specific restrictions
Environmental water exposures never affect immunosuppressed recipients
Hot tub use requires stopping all immunosuppression permanently

explanation.rationale_correct: Transplant programs may provide additional infection-prevention guidelines regarding tap water, water filters, mold exposure, and use of hot tubs.

rationale_incorrect.B: Hot tub and water exposures are addressed in program-specific infection-prevention guidance rather than declared universally safe.
rationale_incorrect.C: Environmental exposures including hot tubs may pose infection risk to immunosuppressed recipients.
rationale_incorrect.D: Infection-prevention teaching addresses environmental exposures; it does not require stopping immunosuppression.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention → vii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: additional infection prevention guidelines regarding … tap water … use of hot tubs

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → e. Infection prevention → vii. (program guidelines on tap water, water filters, mold, hot tubs); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Tenth 010500 item; environmental exposure angle distinct from travel restriction (cctc-1025) and osteopenia (cctc-1047); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.
